name: Ecnoglutide

lead:
Ecnoglutide is a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist developed by Sciwind Biosciences in China. It is given by subcutaneous injection and was approved in China in January 2026 for blood-sugar control in adults with type 2 diabetes and in March 2026 for long-term weight management in adults with obesity or with overweight and a related condition.
Its appearance relevance comes through weight and fat loss, the same route discussed for other GLP-1 drugs: less body fat can mean a leaner body and a slimmer face. A 2025 phase 3 trial in Chinese adults with overweight or obesity compared weekly ecnoglutide with placebo, and Wikipedia summarises weight reductions of roughly 9 to 13 percent over 48 weeks depending on dose.

paras: It is a prescription medicine used alongside diet and physical activity under medical supervision. It is a weekly injection, and an oral tablet formulation is in development. It is a newer drug, and online discussion of it is much smaller than for semaglutide or tirzepatide.

As with other GLP-1 agonists, gastrointestinal side effects are the main class concern in trials. It is available by prescription in China only so far as the sources describe, and use outside of clinical supervision or through unregulated suppliers is not supported by its labelling.

chain: Activates GLP-1 receptors and lowers appetite
Lower body weight and fat mass
angle.text: Weekly ecnoglutide reduced body weight versus placebo in a phase 3 trial of adults with overweight or obesity. Less body fat is what people mean when they discuss GLP-1 drugs for a leaner physique, though the trials report weight rather than appearance.

lead: Ecnoglutide (also XW003) is a lipopeptide GLP-1 receptor agonist developed by Sciwind Biosciences. It is described as a cAMP-biased agonist, meaning it was designed to activate the cyclic AMP signalling pathway more than other signalling pathways at the receptor.[1][2]

A review reports that subcutaneous ecnoglutide received its first approval in China in January 2026 for glycaemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes, followed in March 2026 by approval for long-term weight management in adults with obesity or with overweight and at least one weight-related comorbidity. It is also being evaluated in adolescents with obesity, in obesity with sleep apnoea and in obesity with knee osteoarthritis, and an oral tablet is in development.[1]

In terms of looks, GLP-1 drugs act by reducing appetite and body weight, so the outcome people care about is fat loss and a leaner body composition. Published trials of ecnoglutide measure weight and glucose rather than appearance.
infobox: Subcutaneous injection, once weekly; oral form in development

paras: In China ecnoglutide is approved for glycaemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes and, together with diet control and increased physical activity, for long-term weight management in adults with obesity or with overweight and a weight-related comorbidity.[1]

Ecnoglutide is a long-acting GLP-1 analog whose design was reported in a 2023 discovery paper that described it as cAMP-biased.[3] Biased agonism refers to preferentially engaging one intracellular signalling route; the developers' stated aim is a favourable potency and tolerability profile.

A multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial in 36 centres in China tested once-weekly ecnoglutide in adults aged 18 to 75 with overweight or obesity.[4] Wikipedia summarises the 2025 trial as showing weight reductions of roughly 9 to 13 percent beyond placebo over 48 weeks, depending on dose.[2]

A phase 2 randomised trial of 145 adults with type 2 diabetes tested three weekly doses against placebo over 20 weeks, with change in HbA1c as the primary outcome.[5] Phase 3 trials include EECOH-1 against placebo and EECOH-2, a 52-week non-inferiority comparison with dulaglutide in patients on metformin.[6][7] Meta-analyses of its diabetes efficacy have also been published.[8][9]
A phase 1 study examined whether ecnoglutide affected the pharmacokinetics of rosuvastatin and digoxin in healthy participants.[10]
Ecnoglutide belongs to a wave of incretin-based drugs, and reviews of emerging obesity pharmacotherapies and network meta-analyses compare such agents on weight and safety outcomes.[11][12]

timeline.event: Discovery of ecnoglutide as a cAMP-biased GLP-1 analog reported.[3]
Phase 2 trial in type 2 diabetes published.[5]
Phase 3 obesity trial and EECOH-2 results published.[4][7]
Approved in China for type 2 diabetes (January) and weight management (March).[1]
